newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says to rely on taxes, not foreign aid.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says to rely on taxes, not foreign aid.

text.p: Indonesia believes it should self-fund future development rather than rely on loans from the developed world, the official Antara news agency said on Sunday.
"We have been dependent on foreign loans too long. Now we urgently need to make efforts to lessen that dependence," Director General of Taxes Fuad Bawazier was quoted by the agency as saying.
Fuad said that Indonesia's wealthy should pay more taxes to help finance development.
"Some people still do not understand the need for taxes to finance national development and continue to think taxes are not necessary," he said.
Last month, at U.S.-ASEAN talks, Indonesia said it was concerned by the reduced aid commitment of the United States to southeast Asia.
The United States has said that trade and not aid should be the basis of its future partnership with the rapidly developing ASEAN nations.
In June this year, donor nations pledged about $5.3 billion in development aid to Indonesia for a 12-month period. Donors pledged $5.36 million in 1995 and $5.2 billion a year earlier.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines.
